extracted.intended_audience: general adult readers interested in self-improvement and domestic/social reform (late 19th–early 20th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for improving domestic life and for voluntary 'habit culture' (methods to change habits and develop new virtues). Aimed at individuals (especially women) and households considering organization, specialization, and personal moral training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernization of housekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: “The whole labor of 'housekeeping' will be removed from the home, and the woman will begin to enjoy it as a man does.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home labor should be reorganized/modernized so that housework is reduced or professionalized; results should be a home that is "cleaner, quieter, more sanitary, more beautiful and comfortable, and far less expensive." The passage treats modernized housekeeping as a measurable social good (cleanliness, quiet, sanitation, beauty, comfort, economy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization of women / development of 'Mother-Genius' and 'Domestic Genius'
rubrics_metrics.description: “She will cease to exist. She will become specialized as every civilized person must be. She will not be a woman less, but a human being more... the work of the Mother-Genius and maintained by the Domestic Genius.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates that women should be permitted/encouraged to specialize (domestic and maternal geniuses) rather than remain 'average' in all things. Specialization is framed as raising public health, intellect, and peace of mind; the guideline implies structuring roles and training so individuals can develop distinctive, high-performing domestic skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes of an ideal home
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Home--that should mean to her precisely what it means to him. Peace, comfort, joy and pride; seclusion; mutual companionship; rest, beautiful privacy and rest--not a workshop.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a normative standard for domestic life: homes should provide emotional and physical refuge (peace, comfort, joy, pride, privacy, companionship) rather than functioning as sites of exhaustive labor. The anti-pattern is treating the home as a 'workshop.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for fewer well-born and well-trained children
rubrics_metrics.description: “Better one well-born and well-trained, than the incapable six survivors of the unnecessary twelve.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for quality over quantity in childbearing and rearing: fewer children who are properly trained and cared for are preferable to many poorly reared offspring. This is presented as a social standard for family planning and rearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective action and organization of women
rubrics_metrics.description: “Let them collect then! Let them organize and specialize--the two go together. Let them develop Genius--and use it...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends women address social/domestic problems collectively rather than individually: organize, specialize, and create structures (clubs, cooperative services) to develop and apply domestic skills at scale. Implies organizational remedies (e.g., day labor, clubs, provisioning) for systemic household problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for voluntary habit culture (four-step formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured personal method for acquiring new habits: make up your mind; dismiss the matter; when the determination reappears welcome it and 'drive it in'; then 'turn off the power' and repeat slowly until the habit is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Detailed procedural steps as illustrated with the aim of checking "Thoughtless Speech" and substituting "Conscious Control":
- First Step: Make up your mind (a distinct act of internal determination).
- Second Step: Dismiss the matter from your mind (do not obsess).
- Third Step: When determination reappears, welcome it, remake the determination harder, then dismiss again ('drive it in').
- Fourth Step: Turn off the power for the day; do not think about it further that day. Repeat more often as recurrence intervals shorten until the new nerve-connection is established.
The method emphasizes gradual repetition, internal alarm-setting, and measured reinforcement rather than constant forcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repetition to establish new voluntary control (retraining reflexes)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Reflex action is earlier established than voluntary action... To learn to cut with the left is an extra effort... It is merely a matter of repetition of command, properly measured.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the psychological/physiological rationale: reflexive behaviours dominate; voluntary control requires creating new neural connections. The operational guideline is to use repeated, properly measured commands (practice) to transfer control from reflex to volition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overdoing: practice and rest; 'stop before you are tired'
rubrics_metrics.description: “Practice--and rest; that is the trick... Always before we have been taught to strive unceasingly for our virtues... Stop _before_ you are tired.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning and procedural guidance: do not attempt relentless, exhaustive practice (which leads to regression). Instead use intervals of effort followed by conscious rest; withdraw effort by choice before exhaustion to allow gradual incremental improvement. This is described as the 'patentable secret' of the method and is essential for safe, sustainable habit formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude toward setbacks and 'back-sliding'
rubrics_metrics.description: “Do not scold because it was so long in coming. Do not lament its lateness... When you are learning... go slow... Don't waste energy in fretting over this delay; just renew your determination as often as it pops into your head--'I will think before I speak.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsels a compassionate, patient approach to failures and delays: avoid harsh self-reproach; welcome the recurrence of determination cheerfully; repeatedly renew without self-scolding. Treat lapses as expected parts of the process and conserve energy for steady repetition rather than guilt-driven intense sessions.
